headline: Sign error in the mirror formula
sub: Always apply sign convention: distances measured against the incident ray are negative. Most marks are lost here, not in calculation.
subject: Physics

headline: Forgetting units in numericals
sub: Power in dioptre needs focal length in METRES, not cm. Convert first, then substitute. Missing units = lost marks.
subject: Physics

headline: Mixing up concave and convex correction
sub: Myopia → concave lens. Hypermetropia → convex lens. Remember: myopia and concave both feel 'minus'.
subject: Physics

headline: Not checking the discriminant first
sub: Before solving a quadratic, find D = b² − 4ac. If asked for 'nature of roots', you don't even need to solve.
subject: Maths

headline: Wrong ratio order in section formula
sub: For ratio m:n, the formula is (mx₂ + nx₁)/(m+n). Swapping m and n is the #1 silent mistake.
subject: Maths

headline: Balancing equations: count atoms both sides
sub: A chemical equation must have equal atoms of each element on both sides. Never change formulas — only coefficients.
subject: Chemistry

headline: Board exam tip: attempt by marks, not order
sub: Do the questions you're sure of first. Lock in easy marks before spending time on tough ones.
subject: General

headline: Draw diagrams — they carry marks
sub: In Science, a neat labelled diagram (ray diagram, life process, circuit) often earns marks on its own.
subject: General

headline: Revise formulas daily, not once
sub: Spaced revision beats cramming. Keep a one-page formula sheet and glance at it every day before the exam.
subject: General

headline: Show every step in Maths
sub: CBSE gives step marks. Even if the final answer is wrong, correct steps still score. Never skip working.
subject: Maths

headline: Practice previous years' papers
sub: Many questions repeat in pattern. Solving 5 years of past papers is the single highest-ROI revision method.
subject: General

headline: Read the question twice
sub: Underline what's asked (find, prove, define). Half of all lost marks come from answering the wrong thing.
subject: General
